page: Microsoft Azure D16as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth present certain tradeoffs. While small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is average at 1216.27 GB/sec, large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 38.44 GB/sec, which places it in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is also a bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model rated as poor at 4.47 tokens/sec. Most other operations, including Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation, perform in the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16as_v6 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads that require reliable single-core performance without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core and database performance, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, software compilation, and light database operations. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference due to the identified memory bandwidth and processing bottlenecks.
